lines.trans: Up in Hokkaido we talked big about competing, yet reality is heaven and earth apart.

words.gram: Conjunction trailing off to soften hesitation.

lines.trans: I don't see it that way.
Barking does no good when the reality is that Ikezawa's tapes are the ones selling.
We are only getting started.
When your head feels murky, gulping cheap booze is the best cure.

words.gram: Past た-form of する (to do/happen).

lines.trans: How about it — gotten used to this district a little yet?
Well, little by little.
You've got real business flair; work hard and make me rich again.

words.gram: て-form of 頑張る (work hard), used sarcastically here.
Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).

meanings.note: More formal counterpart of じゃあ used in business and polite conversation.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
In the idiom 口を出す, means 'to meddle / butt in'.
Connects a contrasting fact or trails off at the end of a sentence to voice a polite objection.

examples.text: お風呂に入りましたけど。
examples.trans: I already took a bath, though.

examples.text: 高いけど、おいしいです。
北海道では勝負するって大口たたいてたけど、現実は天と地だな。
examples.trans: Up in Hokkaido we talked big about competing, yet reality is heaven and earth apart.

examples.text: ほえててもしょうがねえだろ、現実は池沢が売れてんだからよ。
examples.trans: Barking does no good when the reality is that Ikezawa's tapes are the ones selling.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 北海道では勝負するって大口たたいてたけど、現実は天と地だな。
examples.trans: Up in Hokkaido we talked big about competing, yet reality is heaven and earth apart.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb describing goods selling on the market without naming a seller.

examples.text: この絵本はよく売れます。
新しい本がたくさん売れました。
examples.trans: Many copies of the new book sold.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: from now on; in the future; now
meanings.note: Time expression referring to the immediate or upcoming future.

examples.text: これから家へ帰ります。

examples.trans: The real test starts from here.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Before an adjective (一番近い), forms the superlative ('closest').

examples.trans: This one is the most popular.

examples.text: 一番近い駅はどこですか。

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 冷蔵庫の中のものがほぼ腐ってて、一カ月ぶりだったんで。
examples.trans: Almost everything inside my fridge had rotted, since it had been a full month.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Casual, blunt contraction of あなた used between intimates or in heated speech.

examples.text: あんたは商才がある。頑張ってまたもうけさせてくれよ。
examples.trans: You've got real business flair; work hard and make me rich again.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: 頑張ります! is the classic cheerful commitment when starting a job or task.

examples.trans: I will do my best today too.
Do your best on the exam!

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

examples.text: 池沢にまたやられるようなヘマだけはすんなよ。

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.
